method: Lexical/source candidate review plus full objective comparison with pilot and earlier batches. Heuristics cannot establish absence of semantic duplication.

records.reason: Rehash-before-verification authenticates the wrong secret; comparing fresh salted hashes rejects a correct secret. Different failure direction and repair ordering.
Named optional argument omission versus initializing a nullable property; shared JSON and null syntax has no shared decision rule.
Skipping default parameters by name versus strict callback-call boundaries; parameter syntax is incidental overlap.
LIKE pattern metacharacters remain interpreted inside a bound value; SQL identifier selection is a different boundary outside value binding.
Blank-row identity versus an omitted escape-argument deprecation. The new fixture explicitly supplies escape and preserves empty and zero fields.
Duplicate-key parser disagreement affects authorization; numeric-key object/array round trips concern representation shape without duplicate members.
Overlapping Fibers share one connection transaction; repeated bindParam executions observe a referenced variable. Neither repair addresses the other defect.
The clone repair must rebind a Closure's private this scope; the old clone question only tracks scalar copies and a shared nested object.
Inherited method declarations share a static slot; separate Closure instances own separate static slots. Different ownership units must be identified.
Array key reindexing versus assignment/logical precedence; compact JSON output causes lexical overlap only.
Restoring graph cycles and enum identity through serialization versus reading enum name/value fields.
Tail slicing with preserved keys and unchanged source versus allowed-field selection by key membership.
Stringable conversion under strict calls versus omitted nullable default arguments. Both use type declarations but fail at different boundaries.
Interface membership versus concrete class name; anonymous declaration identity and shared static state require different reasoning.
Generator send performs implicit startup and resumes a yield; foreach uses a cursor independent of an array's internal pointer.
Lazy proxy forwarding shares a backing object's state while retaining proxy identity; shallow clone copying has no lazy initialization or forwarding.
Static local storage ownership across inherited method bodies versus late static binding of class identity through forwarding calls.
Prepending mixed array keys versus typed-property reference incompatibility; common scalar/JSON syntax is not semantic duplication.
Match evaluates selected conditions/results; recursion prints during call-stack unwinding. The output-order skill is shared but the control mechanism differs.
array_unshift actively renumbers existing keys; append after unset preserves the array's next-index state.
Prepending key renumbering versus fresh default-array values per function call.
Internal pointer independence versus assignment to a by-value foreach variable; a pointer read is essential only in the new question.
A bounded fgets truncates a long record; the pilot discards a valid zero string through truthiness. Different fixtures and fixes.
An invokable object's cumulative callback state versus destructor timing after aliases are unset.
Serialized graph reconstruction preserves cycles and resolves enum singletons; cloning does not reconstruct a graph through serialization.
Pre/postcondition loop execution versus global constant visibility; only small-output boilerplate overlaps.
Integer-key renumbering after insertion versus automatic conversion of canonical numeric-string keys during array construction.
Interface type membership versus numeric-string key normalization; unrelated semantic rules.
Array internal pointer state versus shallow object cloning; shared diagnostic output syntax is incidental.
A retained callable accumulates state across invocations; cloning copies outer state but shares a nested object. No clone exists in the new fixture.
Failed dynamic initialization is retried; separate Closure objects retain independently initialized static locals. Exception timing is essential only in 0225.
Lazy proxy forwards to an already existing object; a lazy ghost excludes one property from initialization. Identity forwarding and initialization exclusion differ.
Object-handle mutation plus local rebinding versus a scalar reference parameter coercing the caller's storage.
String containment with an empty needle versus loop entry conditions; boolean JSON output is common scaffolding.
Interface satisfaction and concrete class lookup versus clone identity and nested-object sharing.
Cascading text substitution versus pre/postcondition loops; output pairs do not imply duplicate behavior.
Boolean text validation with null-on-failure versus numeric-string array-key conversion.
Invokable callback reuse accumulates state across array_map and direct calls; simple object assignment tests aliasing without callable behavior.
Graph serialization and enum singleton identity versus converting a posted scalar to an allowed enum case.
Loop entry timing versus unary-minus/exponentiation grouping.
Prepending mixed keys renumbers integers; recursive replacement retains positions and can overwrite with null.
Prepending to one map versus zipping unequal arrays through null-callback array_map.
Interface membership/concrete class identity versus enum name/backing scalar.
Serialization builds a new cyclic graph; proxy initialization forwards to an existing graph object. Identity is tested through different mechanisms.
Selecting the parent method body versus late-bound lookup of an overridden class constant in a factory.
Callable invocation retains an accumulator; ghost initialization separates raw non-lazy writes from lazy state.
Interface type tests versus indirect mutation of overloaded array and object values.
Type membership and class naming versus loop entry; JSON pairs create incidental overlap.
Stringable coercion versus trait alias visibility; the access/type failures have different triggers and repairs.
Returning from a redirect helper resumes its caller; finally mutates an object already selected for return. No cleanup mutation occurs in 0257.
Parallel-column sort ordering versus function default-array freshness.
Proxy-backed state versus independent array cursors; no common control or data transformation.
Property forwarding to a backing object versus state accumulated through __invoke callbacks.
Loop conditions versus integer-string key normalization.
Array numeric-key renumbering versus object assignment aliasing.
Interface satisfaction versus shared object handles after assignment; no mutation/alias trace is needed in 0208.
Interface membership versus unmatched match throwing; unrelated type/control rules.
Value sorting while preserving keys versus set intersection using string representations. Both retain keys but require different comparison operations.
An object parameter's property mutation survives local rebinding; a by-value scalar foreach assignment leaves the source array unchanged.
Interface membership versus resolving same-named private fields under a bound Closure scope.
Concrete class identity versus late-static forwarding across method calls.
Interface contract checks versus lazy initialization bypass for one property.
Array cursor independence versus automatic next append index after removal.
foreach's internal cursor versus an explicit reference-returning function storage binding.
A failed static initializer retries before persistence; an invokable object's state changes on every callback invocation.
A second decode invalidates a representation check; a request-derived Host was never trusted provenance. Canonicalization and source trust are different boundaries.
Loop-entry condition timing versus anonymous-class declaration identity.
Fallthrough after a case is selected versus loose switch selection compared with strict match. Different phase of switch evaluation.
Interface membership versus shallow readonly restrictions on a referenced object.
Concrete type lookup versus static state shared across object instances.
Match side-effect evaluation order versus enum name/value access.
Callable object accumulator state versus array cursor state; neither behavior is an alias for the other.
Generator yield/send/return channels versus copying or binding a returned reference.
Lazy proxy identity remains distinct from its backing object; interface membership does not involve proxy initialization.
Serialized graph cycles and enum identity versus type membership and class naming.
A helper's return is local to that function; include/require differ in missing-file diagnostics and exception control flow.
Rethrowing must preserve exact exception identity; retry classification searches exception causes with an outer permanent barrier.
Missing-file include/require flow versus case sensitivity of function and variable names.
Multiset removal preserves remaining duplicate values; exact CRLF removal preserves payload bytes. Different data models and operations despite the word remove.
Removing one list occurrence versus a property hook's stored value differing from an assignment expression.
Pre/postcondition loops versus late-static forwarding class scope.
A local object parameter is rebound after mutating the caller's object; cloning copies scalar state and shares a nested object without parameter rebinding.
Interface membership versus deliberately exported references bypassing later restricted-write checks.
